newsitem.title: USA: NFL, AMERICAN FOOTBALL-OWNERS VOTE DOWN INSTANT REPLAY.
newsitem.headline: NFL, AMERICAN FOOTBALL-OWNERS VOTE DOWN INSTANT REPLAY.

text.p: National Football League owners have voted down a proposal to bring back instant replay.

The proposal to use videotape to review certain refereeing decisions fell three votes short during the NFL owners' meetings Wednesday. Twenty of the 30 owners voted for the plan, with 23 needed for approval.

The NFL Competition Committee, co-chaired by Green Bay Packers coach Mike Holmgren and New York Giants general manager George Young, presented a proposal to reinstate instant replay for the upcoming season. A proposal to bring back instant replay also failed in 1992.

Under the new proposal, each team was to get a maximum of two replays per game, but each challenge would result in the removal of a timeout, regardless of whether the play was overturned. That provision appeared to be the backbreaker.
Coaches were fearful that they could be left without a timeout to call for a replay challenge in the final seconds of a game.

The replay proposal included four types of reviewable plays: any or all scoring plays, sideline plays in or out of bounds, number of players on the field and fumbles or interceptions. Judgment calls on possible pass interference plays would not be subject to review.
The NFL experimented with instant replay by using a sideline monitor in selected pre-season games last year.

Also on Wednesday, the league reached a decision on the thorny issue of cross ownership. NFL Commissioner Paul Tagliabue announced approval of a plan to allow an NFL owner to acquire an interest in a baseball, basketball, or hockey team in the owner's own market or in a neutral area.
The vote directly affected the Miami Dolphins and Seattle Seahawks.

Dolphins owner Wayne Huizenga also owns Major League Baseball's Florida Marlins and the National Hockey League's Florida Panthers. Paul Allen, who owns the NBA's Portland Trail Blazers, is in the process of acquiring the Seahawks.
Expansion also was to be discussed at the meetings, which were to conclude Thursday. Tagliabue has said he wants the league "to take a hard look at expansion to 32 teams."
The NFL has promised to put a team back in Cleveland for the 1999 season. The league also would prefer to put a franchise back in Los Angeles, which lost both the Rams and Raiders.
